name: timezone-rule
note: The suspected root cause, isolated. `start` and `timezone` are both required and non-nullable in the schema, so an event a source states without a zone cannot be expressed — while the system prompt forbids anything evidence does not support. Refusal is the only output satisfying both. This says what to put in `timezone` when the source is silent, and changes nothing else. If this alone moves 0/7 to 7/7, the diagnosis holds and the shipped fix is a prompt line plus a receipt.
instructionTemplate: Return the closed event result JSON contract. Evidence spans must address the supplied private fragments. Output has exactly version, requestId, outcome, code, detail, duplicatePolicy, confirmationState, and events; never echo fragment documents. Start MUST be a full ISO 8601 datetime. When the source states a date and a time, use them. When the source states a place but no timezone, use the IANA timezone of that place. When the source states neither a timezone nor a place, use UTC and say so in detail. A missing timezone is never a reason to withhold an event. End is null when the source does not state one; location is null when the source does not name one. Extract every named activity that has an explicit date and time. For those events set outcome to succeeded, confirmationState to pending, and every event confirmation to pending. Only when no named activity has an explicit date and time, set outcome to refused, code to no-event-supported, confirmationState to refused, and events to the empty array. Partial is only for a nonempty event list when some source evidence could not be fully processed. {{UNTRUSTED_CONTENT}}
